precepts.why: Bernice married her uncle Herod of Chalcis and was with her brother Herod Agrippa II at Paul's trial, and one of them came in with great pomp. “And on the morrow, when Agrippa was come, and Bernice, with great pomp,” Great pomp, meaning what? The band was playing, music was blasting everywhere, people were throwing flowers and roses; they made a big spectacle of these two. “and was entered into the place of hearing, with the chief captains, and principal men of the city, at Festus’ commandment Paul was brought forth.” So the scholars know that these people are Jewish converts. It is only black people in the Christian church, black and brown, that don't know; we are confused: everybody's the same in Jesus, baby, we're all the same. Oh, shut the hell up, grandma.

points: Paul said, I stand at Caesar's judgment seat, where I ought to be judged. If I be an offender, or have committed anything worthy of death, I refuse not to die; but if there be none of these things whereof these accuse me, no man may deliver me unto them. I appeal unto Caesar. Festus answered, Hast thou appealed unto Caesar? Unto Caesar shalt thou go. So Paul found it better to be judged by the Romans than by the wicked Israelites, because those Pharisees wanted Paul put to death.
